name: French Defense
description: A practical French course that teaches the main e6-d5 structure first, then simple responses to White deviations.

branches.title: Main Line: e6 and d5

moves.title: White claims center
moves.explanation: White takes space and opens lines. e4 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. The French teaches pawn chains: Black attacks the base with c5, while White uses space and piece activity.

moves.title: Prepare d5
moves.explanation: e6 supports d5 and builds the French pawn chain. e6 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. The French teaches pawn chains: Black attacks the base with c5, while White uses space and piece activity.

moves.title: White expands
moves.explanation: White creates a big pawn center. d4 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. The French teaches pawn chains: Black attacks the base with c5, while White uses space and piece activity.

moves.title: Challenge center
moves.explanation: d5 attacks e4 with support. This is the core French idea. d5 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. The French teaches pawn chains: Black attacks the base with c5, while White uses space and piece activity.

moves.title: Develop to c3
moves.explanation: Nc3 develops a knight to c3. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: Develop to c6

moves.title: Develop to e7
moves.explanation: Nge7 develops a knight to e7. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: Improve with h3
moves.explanation: h3 is a quiet improving move. Quiet moves matter when they finish development, prevent counterplay, or prepare a clear next plan.

moves.title: Trade or capture on d4
moves.explanation: cxd4 introduces a practical trade. Before trading, ask what improves afterward: an open file, a safer king, a damaged pawn structure, or the removal of an active enemy piece.

hints: Follow the highlighted move and say the idea out loud.
After each move, check king safety, center control, and piece activity.
When a trade appears, ask what file opens and which piece improves next.
coachingNotes: The French teaches pawn chains: Black attacks the base with c5, while White uses space and piece activity.
Good trades usually remove an active enemy piece, open a useful file, or simplify once your king is safe.
After the opening, do not drift: improve your worst piece, connect rooks, and look for one clear pawn break.

ideas: Challenge White's center before it rolls forward.
Look for c5 later as a second break.
The French teaches pawn chains: Black attacks the base with c5, while White uses space and piece activity.
Trade only when it improves your position, removes danger, or opens a useful file.
By move 8-12, you should know your early middlegame plan: safe king, active pieces, and one central break.
commonMistakes: Playing passively after building the pawn chain.
Stopping after memorized moves and playing without a plan.
Trading automatically without asking what improves afterward.
Starting an attack before castling or finishing development.
